title: Transient tenant isolation breach during Dedicated onboarding when overlapping pod CIDRs reused
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: A customer (FinSight Analytics) onboarding from Private -> Dedicated experienced a transient tenant isolation breach during CIDR reassignment. Symptoms: DNS replies and short-lived TCP flows from the new tenant were observed reaching an unrelated tenant for ~90s during a scheduled migration window. Impact: production requests for two customers experienced incorrect routing and 5xx failures; escalated by Support.
root_cause: IPAM allocator reused a /24 pod CIDR immediately after a tenant cleanup job marked the prefix as free, but the overlay VNI/VTEP mapping and route-programming had not finished deallocation on the host fleet. Due to an ordering race, the new tenant's overlay traffic was accepted by still-bound VTEPs for the previous tenant until route reconciliation completed. Additionally, a gap in the allocator's lease-state machine allowed immediate reassign rather than put into a quarantine TTL. This produced transient asymmetric paths where replies used stale ARP/flow state on other hosts.
fix_summary: 1) Add a 'quarantine' lease-state to IPAM: prefixes freed enter QUARANTINE for configurable TTL (default 5 minutes) before reallocation. 2) Extend deallocation handshake: host agent now waits for explicit route/ARP/VTEP drain ack from all hosts before marking deallocated. 3) Add sanity check in control plane: prevent allocation if VNI/VTEP mapping still referenced. 4) Emergency patch to rollback automatically if flow leakage detected during migrations. 5) Backfill automated e2e tests for onboarding path and add unit tests for lease-state machine.
rollback_plan: Feature guard with FF_IPAM_QUARANTINE=false allows reverting quarantine semantics. Emergency rollback steps: 1) disable new allocator path via feature flag; 2) re-trigger route reconciliation on hosts; 3) if necessary, move impacted customers to maintenance window with BGP/peering quiesce. Rollback doc: https://confluence.internal.redwood/dedicated/onboarding-rollback
verification_steps: Run dedicated-onboarding e2e suite against staging with overlapping prefix simulation
Simulate rapid free->allocate cycles and assert QUARANTINE prevents immediate reuse
Deploy to canary zone, run 5000 synthetic DNS/TCP flows during a staged migration and monitor cross-tenant flow counters
Validate route/arp drain ack log entries on host agents and central controller
monitoring_updates: Added metric: ipam.quarantine.alloc_blocked_count; Added alert: alert_ipam_quarantine_breached(p95>0 for 10m) and alert: tenant_cross_tenant_flow_detected(rate>5/min). Dashboards: new 'IPAM & Onboarding' panel on infra-summary.
postmortem: Timeline: 2026-02-09 02:10 UTC - Support escalated after customer noticed failed requests. 02:25 - Eng oncall reproduced issue in staging. 05:00 - Root cause identified as IPAM lease-state race. 2026-02-10 18:30 - Fix deployed to canary; 2026-02-12 09:00 - fix rolled to all Dedicated zones. Actions: code changes (PR #8571), new e2e tests, updated runbook for onboarding, added customer notification templates. Customer remediation: data requests reconciled and compensating ops performed. No data exfiltration detected.
comments: 2026-02-09 - Maya Chen: Ticket created after oncall reproducer showed cross-tenant DNS replies in staging. Initial hypothesis: conntrack/host agent lingering flows.
2026-02-09 - Priya Nambiar: Confirmed reproducer. Collated logs from two affected hosts and observed immediate reallocation events from IPAM service logs.

2026-02-10 - Rahul Singh (networking): Found allocator emitted 'ALLOCATED' for freed prefix without waiting for drain ack. Experimented with adding 60s delay - mitigated but not acceptable latency. Switched to quarantine TTL approach.
2026-02-11 - QA: Added focused test that drives allocate/free cycles at 200 ops/min and asserts no cross-tenant flows; flaky reproduction fixed after adding explicit VTEP reference count checks.
2026-02-12 - Release: Canary rollout to us-west-2 with FF_IPAM_QUARANTINE=true. Observed no further cross-tenant flow metrics in canary. Rolling to prod on 2026-02-12 09:00.
2026-02-15 - Support: Customer FinSight provided validation that traffic normalized; issued customer postmortem and crediting.
2026-02-20 - Security: Confirmed no auth bypass or data leakage. Recommended additional audit logging around VTEP assignments.
